title: Operator pocket cheatbook + telemetry snippets — 48h rollout
content:
Purpose and intent:
This is a concise operator-facing cheatbook to carry through a 48-hour rapid rollout (canary -> regional ramp -> global). Focus is: what to watch, quick remediation steps, exact telemetry queries, and an abbreviated release-notes template operators can paste to incident channels. This is intentionally terse — print/save to pocket.

Scope:
- Target release: infra/model-routing v2.11 (canary)
- Window: 48h rolling ramp starting 2027-11-06 00:00 UTC
- Primary regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1

High-level decision rules (TL;DR):
- Green: canary good if latency p50 < 85ms, error_rate < 0.2% for 30m and token-throughput within 10% of baseline
- Yellow: any metric in middle band or single-region spike — throttle traffic and extend canary dwell by +60m
- Red: sustained >1% client errors OR p95 latency > 400ms for 15m -> trigger rollback to previous canary image + open incident channel and paging list

Operator checklist (pre-rollout, 2h before):
[ ] Verify release bundle checksum (sha256) matches RL-9072
[ ] Confirm canary infra is provisioned: 2 g4dn nodes per region (canary pool)
[ ] Sanity smoke: run smoke script against canary endpoint (smoke.sh) -> must return 200 and expected tokens
[ ] Confirm dashboards loaded: "Canary Overview", "Routing Latency Lens", "Error Budget"
[ ] Notify observers in #releases and #oncall-ops channels with ETA
[ ] Ensure fallback route (model-v2.10-fallback) is available and warmed

48h rollout calendar (compact):
- T-00:00 (canary start): route 1% traffic to canary, start detailed sampling
- T+00:30: automated telemetry snapshot + manual ops check
- T+01:00: if green -> 5% traffic; else hold/rollback per decision rules
- T+03:00: 20% traffic in target region if stable 2h
- T+08:00: 50% traffic in region; start parallel ramp to next region
- T+24:00: target 100% for first two regions if stable; begin global ramp windows (10% per region every 1h)
- T+36:00: stabilization watch, sampling retention extended to 2h windows
- T+48:00: finalize rollout, promote image to stable tags, publish release notes

Quick telemetry queries (copy-paste):
- Canary p50/p95 latency (PromQL):
  sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"canary|stable",job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, deployment)
  // use dashboard lens for percentile calc; or: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{deployment="canary",handler!~"/health"}[5m])) by (le))

- Token throughput (tokens/s):
  sum(rate(model_tokens_generated_total{model=~"routing-v.*"}[1m])) by (deployment, region)

- Error rate (5m):
  (sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2..",deployment="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{deployment="canary"}[5m]))) * 100

- KV cache hit ratio (useful for latency regressions):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{deployment="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{deployment="canary"}[5m]))

Alert thresholds to watch (ops-fast):
- CanaryErrorHigh: error_rate_canary > 0.5% for 5m -> paging P1
- LatencySpike: p95_canary > 500ms for 10m -> page P1
- TokenDrop: tokens_canary drops >30% vs baseline 15m mean -> page P2

Immediate remediation recipes (fast path):
- Observed: p95 spike correlated with cache misses
  Steps: 1) verify cache nodes healthy (kubectl get po -l app=kv-cache -o wide); 2) if disk pressure restart cache pods one at a time; 3) temporarily route 80% away from canary; 4) file postmortem ticket.

- Observed: spike in 5xx from a specific region
  Steps: 1) isolate by routing policy: set region weight = 0 for that region; 2) re-run smoke and replay failing requests sample via replayer; 3) if cluster-level problem, scale up nodes; 4) if app-level, rollback.

Rollback quick commands (k8s + routing):
- Promote fallback rule (CLI): rcli routing set-weight --policy release-48h --region us-west1 --model routing-v2.10 --weight 100
- Rollback deploy: kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-router --namespace=canary --to-revision=previous

Abbreviated release-notes template (operator copy-paste):
Title: model-routing v2.11 — rapid canary (2027-11-06)
Summary: Incremental routing updates to improve tail latency and soft-handoff behavior. Canary rolled in us-west1 and eu-west1 starting 2027-11-06 UTC.
Observed: Initial canary showed stable p50/p95 and reduced token cost. Minor transient p95 spikes in ap-southeast1 at T+3h (investigating).
Action: No customer-impacting degradation observed. Rolling to remaining regions subject to green signal.
Notes: Fallback image: routing-v2.10 available; contact on-call if any sustained error budget burn.

Operator pocket snippets for incident channel (short):
- TL;DR: canary -> green at 5% in us-west1; watch p95 and errors. If p95>400ms for 15m -> rollback.
- Link dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/canary-overview
- Pager: @oncall-releases (primary), @sre-ops (secondary)

Investigations & debug tips (shorthand):
- If latency increases but errors stable: dump KV cache metrics, check network egress on node, sample model latency distributions by trace id (use trace id sampler).
- If error codes 429 increase: check token throttling & batching changes; reduce batch sizes or enable short-lived throttles.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we add a synthetic load test at T+02:30 to validate long-tail under 20k rps? (Marco)
- Confirm if model warm-start conflicts with autoscaler cooldowns in ap-southeast1 (Lina)
- Add one-line revert alias to rcli for faster rollback (Ethan)

Post-rollout steps (after T+48h):
[ ] Run 24h post-roll telemetry diff vs baseline (latency, errors, cost per token)
[ ] Rotate canary tag to stable and push changelog to confluence
[ ] Draft full release notes with root-cause details for any anomalies
[ ] Schedule 2-week follow-up retro if any yellow/red events occurred

Appendix: common quicklinks
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/canary-overview
- Routing changelog RL-9072: https://confluence.redwood.internal/RELEASE/RL-9072
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2334
- Pager rota: https://oncall.redwood.internal/team/release-engineering

End notes: keep this doc minimal and evolve into a final runbook if this rollout pattern becomes repeated. If you copy this to a private binder, update small-items TODOs and the cheat alias commands.
